The test image shows a corn stalk/leaf midrib with a reddish-brown stripe containing discrete black dots (likely fungal structures). The surrounding leaf blade has yellowish flecking. Top candidates: Anthracnose (black acervuli in reddish lesions), Physoderma Brown Spot, Physoderma Stalk Rot.

Now I'll view one reference per candidate class.

This Physoderma Brown Spot reference is a strong match — reddish-purple coloration with dark black spots on the stalk, very similar to the test image. Let me check Physoderma Stalk Rot to differentiate.
Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dark spots on green stalk without the reddish background — less similar to test image. For my 4th view, I'll check Purple_Leaf_Sheath to rule it out.

Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows a brown/tan lesion with purple edges — no discrete black spots, clearly different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: corn stalk/midrib with a reddish-purple stripe containing discrete black dots, yellowish flecking on surrounding leaf blade
- **Physoderma Brown Spot** reference (Corn_Disease_109): near-identical pattern — reddish-purple coloration at the node with embedded dark black spots
- Physoderma Stalk Rot: dark spots on green stalk, no reddish background — weaker match
- Anthracnose: stalk rot with broad dark lesions, no comparable stripe + discrete dots pattern
- Purple_Leaf_Sheath: tan/brown irregular lesions, no black spots — ruled out

The reddish-purple node lesion with discrete black sporangial spots is the classic signature of Physoderma Brown Spot.
